steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Place roast in a roasting pan; cover pan. Cook in the preheated oven until beef falls apart and shreds easily, about 2 hours.
Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion; cook until translucent.

Stir chili sauce and vinegar into onion. Fill empty chili sauce bottle with water, shake, and pour liquid into skillet. Stir in garlic, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard powder, black pepper, salt, and cayenne pepper; cook over low heat, stirring often, until thickened.
Shred beef using 2 forks; stir into sauce and simmer for 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Barbecue Beef for Sandwiches
raw_recipe.description: This barbecue beef sandwich recipe starts with pot-roasted beef, shredded and simmered in a hot, spicy sauce — serve on toasted, buttered hamburger buns.

In this video, learn how to make these sandwiches, served on toasted, buttered hamburger buns. Enjoy this savory meal that's perfect for gatherings or a hearty dinner.

review.reviewBody: We used the slow cooker method mentioned by someone else (4 hrs in cooker, plus 1 hr with sauce) and it turned out excellent! Shredding the meat was messy but once I let it cool a bit it was much easier.

This recipe is delicious. The only things I did differently were to season and sear the roast, add a bit of unsalted beef stock and half a sliced onion, and cut back on the salt in the sauce. Otherwise, perfect.

This is a good basic sauce to make and use for pulled pork, chicken, turkey, as well as beef, or (add some chili powder and bell pepper) for a sloppy joe. Really nice for a ham BBQ, too. Or brush on for any BBQ'd meat.

One thing this recipe overlooks is to deglaze the roasting pan and add those juices and browned bits to the sauce. Do that! Especially for a roasted meat.

My roast was only 2 1/2 lbs, so I don't know if this sauce is really enough for 4 lbs. You might want to make more if you like it saucy.

I used one roast that was about 2.5-3lbs and the sauce was just enough. I cooked the roast in the crock pot all day with beef bouillon, onion and garlic powders which gave the meat some flavor. Then I took it out and shredded it and then made the sauce. I also used a ladle of the broth from the meat in the sauce. And I did add some Jack Daniels original BBQ sauce as well to increase the barbecue flavor and it was so good. My husband and I couldn't eat enough of it. It was challenging to leave some for dinner the next night! I will make this very often!

This was really fabulous, everyone including picky eaters loved it!I cooked the roast in a crock pot from frozen on high for approx. 5 hours and then lowered to the low setting while I prepared the sauce. I was forced to change some ingredients since I live in the country and can't run to the store quickly, I used a combo of tomato ketchup and cocktail sauce to replace the chili sauce, but they interchange well and all in all I don't think this changed the recipe by very much. Since the cocktail sauce has horseradish in it I omitted the cayenne pepper. Also, I couldn't bear to have all that juice from the roast go to waste so instead of water I used the broth. Thank you for this delicious recipe.

This recipe is very similar to a recipe from my mothers recipe box - it's old enough that it predates crockpots. But over the years I've made the transition and wanted to share some thoughts and suggestions.
If you're going to put a chuck roast in a crock, sear it well first. Seals in flavor and adds a little texture. You can place your roast on a bed of potato chunks and they'll end up nicely flavored and the juices will surround the meat on all sides. By all means, add your sauce at the beginning! We usually serve it as a roast for the first meal. For the second meal we shred it for sandwiches. Finally, whatever is left gets mixed (with any remaining sauce) with al dente egg noodles. Let the sauce cook in to finish cooking them.
I made 1 recipe of the sauce to see how the flavor was, knowing I would need to make more and could make "corrections" for our tastes there. I thought it was a little vinegary but you need that acid to tenderize the meat. I found the answer to be lemon juice. I reduced the vinegar overall by about a third and added that amount of lemon juice. For us, that was perfect! Thank you for sharing!

Used 3 lbs of pot roast beef, cooked in slowcooker for approx five hours on high with cup of beef broth in the bottom. Made sauce as directed, found it to be enough for 3 lbs of beef. However I added a bit extra beef broth to increase sauce amount. Would definitly double the sauce recipe if I used more meat. used beef broth instead of water to fill up the chili sauce jar... very good! I give the sauce five stars but think a slow cooker is best for meat that is easy to shred. I think I will use this on my pulled pork as well, can't wait to see what the leftovers taste like tonight!

I had a 2. 1/4 lb roast and put in crockpot on high for 4 hours, 15 minutes-shredded easily. I cooked half the sauce on the stove as written but kept the 2 tbsp of brown sugar - I wish I had made more because it was delicious! We felt we needed more sauce so added some Sweet Baby Ray’s but next time I will just make more sauce! We really enjoyed this on buttered and toasted burger buns! Thank you!

I followed the advice of one of the other reviews and put the roast and onions in a crock pot. I used a can of beef broth and cooked on high for 4 hrs. I followed the remainder of the recipe as instructed. Two thumbs up. Has a sweet taste with a bite on the back end. Delicious!

This is good barbecue as is, but to make it better, I did what others had suggested and used some broth from cooking the roast (I did mine in a crockpot on high for about 4-1/2 hours to 5 hours.) instead of the water. I also added some diced pickled jalepenos. My husband said it needed more barbecue taste so I added about a fourth cup of Bulls Eye barbecue sauce. After doctoring it up a bit it was 5 stars.

Great recipe. I had about 4 pounds of chuck roast, and there was no way that this made 16 servings- but it was still delicious! I followed the recipe exactly, making the roast in the oven, but I added beef broth and chopped onion to the pan while roasting. Two hours wasn't quite long enough to make this tender, so I added another 45 minutes to the cooking time. I made the sauce exactly, but in the end, I used my immersion blender to make it smooth (bits of onion and garlic would not go over well with some of my family members). I cooked and shredded the beef ahead of time, and then added it to my slow cooker. I poured the sauce over all, and refrigerated overnight. The next day, I reheated on low. It was perfect. It was also the perfect amount of sauce. Doubling it would have been too much.

We had leftover roast and I wanted to use it in different ways. I made this and it turned out great. Very spicy, sweet, and was a great way to eat leftovers in another meal way. Made open-faced sandwiches.

My chuck roast has been in the slow cooker for 5.5 hours and is still too tough to pull apart with the double forks. I haven't tasted it yet.....gonna keep slow cooking for a while longer....fingers crossed.

Made it as the recipe states. It's SO GOOD! I made a double batch so my husband & I (plus company) could dig into it all weekend while working outside. Every time we reheated it, I heard high accolades. Saving this recipe for years to come!
This is now my go to recipe for shredded beef sandwiches. Whenever I make this. I am asked for the recipe! Its super easy to make and is really good on club rolls!
The Is unbelievably delicious. Next time I would have less sauce or more shredded beef. Otherwise this is wonderful and we will make it again.

This is an awesome recipe! I made it in the slow cooker. Layered 1/2 the onion, then the chuck roast, the other 1/2 of the onion and lastly poured the liquid over everything. Cooked on Low for 7 hours, took the roast out and shredded with a fork, put the roast back in and cooked for one more hour. Only change I would make is not to add the extra chili sauce bottle of water. It's really not needed and made the barbeque a little wet. My husband loved this beef and has requested I make it again.

I made this recipe, and my family loved it. I did not have a chuck roast, but instead used the sauce to cook a sirloin roast which was pre-sliced. I did not shred it, but served the meat with veggies and rice pilaf. I will use this recipe over and over because we all agreed that it was amazing.

This was delicious. I especially liked that it called for putting the garlic in raw, which made the garlic flavor much more pronounced. One thing I did differently was that instead of putting water into the chili sauce bottle to shake it up and get all the sauce out, I just put the 3 Tbsp of vinegar in and shook it up, not adding any water. Didn't require much more cooking to make it nice and thick.
We loved this. I would cook it in the oven for three hours instead of two but the flavor was the best! I made it just as the recipe called.
